key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel, outperforming the other tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: This coating is a promising option for protecting SA516 boiler steel against high-temperature oxidation.
method: Applied Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing linked improved oxidation resistance to dense protective oxides, reduced porosity, and enhanced microhardness, while bare steel showed severe oxide spalling and cracking.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory cycles does not establish long-term durability under actual boiler combustion gases and thermal stresses.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
